Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading: dual listings and the Global Listing Board

Second Reading7 May 2026 bill-800

A Bill at Second Reading, moved by Mr Chee Hong Tat on behalf of the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, that introduces a framework for dual listings between SGX and eligible overseas exchanges and makes other amendments to the Securities and Futures Act.

The Bill is intended to let issuers use one prospectus and harmonised rules to list concurrently on SGX and an overseas exchange, starting with the Global Listing Board with Nasdaq, and to reduce compliance costs. It also allows issuers to engage retail investors using preliminary prospectuses, subject to safeguards, and clarifies that the company issuing underlying shares, not the depositary, lodges the prospectus for depositary receipt offerings. The record says investors will also gain access to a broader range of high-quality investment opportunities and that Singapore investors will continue to be able to seek recourse for losses arising from such breaches under the investor recourse provisions in the SFA.

Open questions from this debate (10)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Which specific issuers have expressed interest in listing on the GLB?
  • How many companies are estimated to be eligible for the GLB under the $2 billion threshold?
  • What are the detailed operational arrangements for settlement, closing and price stabilisation across Nasdaq and SGX?
  • What will the exact text of the MAS regulations under Part 13A contain?
  • Will there be a tiered threshold or review mechanism for the $2 billion market capitalisation requirement?
  • Will future dual listing arrangements with other exchanges have separate thresholds or separate boards?
  • What specific investor-education measures will accompany earlier access to preliminary prospectuses?
  • What key performance indicators will be used to assess whether the GLB delivers sustained liquidity and price discovery?
  • Will Parliament have a role in scrutinising future overseas exchanges before they are designated?
  • How will cross-border enforcement and investor recourse operate where an issuer's management, assets or evidence are located overseas?

CPF (Amendment) Bill — transfer of Singtel Special Discounted Shares to CDP accounts

Second Reading7 May 2026 bill-801

A Bill at Second Reading that amends the CPF Act to enable the transfer of Singtel Special Discounted Shares from the CPF Board to CDP accounts of SDS holders.

The Bill enables the transfer of Singtel SDS from the CPF Board to CDP accounts for around 615,000 SDS holders, planned for November 2026. Holders with individual CDP accounts will have their shares transferred there, while those without will have designated CDP accounts created under their names. Holders may sell and receive proceeds in their CPF Ordinary Account or in cash, with CPF withdrawal conditions waived from 8 April 2026.

  • Whether the CPF Investment Scheme for the Special Account will be closed or the Special Account renamed.

Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill debated and read a Third time

Second Reading, Committee stage, and Third Reading7 May 2026 bill-799

A Bill at Second Reading, the Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill, making miscellaneous amendments to several Acts, including BCA, URA, COTMA, Architects Act, Professional Engineers Act, HDB Act, Wildlife Act and Endangered Species Act.

The record says the Bill expands BCA's functions to manage programmes such as the Estate Upgrading Programme for private residential estates and the Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme, and expands URA's role to coordinate transport, utilities and other infrastructure planning. It also validates past fees and charges collected by BCA, HDB, NParks and URA, raises maximum penalties for wildlife feeding, and changes rules for professional registration and hybrid plants. The record does not set out the aggregate number of people affected or total sums involved in the validated fees.

What happens next The Bill was read a Second time, amendments to clauses 2 and 20 were moved in Committee, and the Bill was read a Third time; the Ayes had it. MND will move a Notice of Amendment at Committee stage to update the title of the SDCPA in clauses 2(e) and 20(11) when the Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Act 2026 comes into operation. Minister Chee said MND will try to share data on the quantum subsequently.

Bill to align competition rules for Singapore's media and telecom sectors

Second Reading7 May 2026 bill-798

A Bill at Second Reading that amends the Info-communications Media Development Authority Act to harmonise competition rules for the telecommunications and media sectors and strengthen IMDA's regulatory toolkit.

The Bill is intended to protect consumer interests by keeping the media market competitive and fair, with public confidence, good content, reasonable prices and a vibrant information environment. It also gives IMDA tools to act when fair market conduct is threatened and where service providers' actions may hurt consumer interests. The transcript also notes that workers may face disruption from mergers or restructurings, and that MOM frameworks and union engagement continue.

  • Mr Lee Hong Chuang

    • Mr Lee Hong Chuang rose to support the Bill.

      Verbatim12 words

      Verbatim16 words

Adjournment Motion on Curiosity Credits 2.0 for secondary school students

Adjournment Motion7 May 2026 matter-adj-2983

An Adjournment Motion speech by Mr David Hoe proposing Curiosity Credits 2.0 for secondary school students, followed by a response from Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi, before Parliament adjourned.

The record does not set out the practical impact.

  • Mr David Hoe

    • Mr David Hoe proposed Curiosity Credits 2.0 to help secondary school students make more informed post-secondary school choices.

      Verbatim26 words
      today, I want to build on this idea and focus on Curiosity Credits 2.0 – helping secondary school students to make more informed post-secondary school choices.

    • He asked whether MOE can study and pilot a more structured way to help students who learn best through experience.

      Verbatim24 words
      I would, therefore, like to ask whether MOE can study and pilot a more structured way to help students who learn best through experience.

    • Under the proposal, from Secondary 1 onwards students would have a Curiosity Credits wallet.

      Verbatim16 words
      From Secondary 1 onwards, students would have this thing that I call a Curiosity Credits wallet.

    • The taster sessions would be designed by ITEs, polytechnics, universities or specialised institutions, and schools could bring them into classrooms or students could attend them at institutions during protected exposure periods.

      Verbatim42 words
      These taster sessions are designed by ITEs, polytechnics, universities or specialised institutions, and schools can bring these tasters into the school and into the classrooms during selected weeks and also allow students to attend them at these institutions during protected exposure periods.

    • He said the aim is structured exposure, not an open-ended voucher scheme.

      Verbatim18 words
      The aim here is not to create an open-ended voucher scheme. The aim is to provide structured exposure.

    • He set a target that by Secondary 4 students could have about six to eight structured taster experiences in different clusters.

      Verbatim26 words
      if by Secondary 4, they can have about six to eight structured taster experiences in different clusters, this might help them to make a better decision.

    • He proposed safeguards including that it should not be cash but credits and entitlement used for approved programmes.

      Verbatim16 words
      First, it should not be cash. It should be credits and entitlement used for approved programmes.

    • He said the issue is fit, not whether junior college, polytechnic or ITE is better.

      Verbatim16 words
      The issue is not whether junior college, polytechnic or ITE is better. The issue is fit.

  • Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi

    • Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi said MOE is open to ideas like Mr Hoe's that can bolster existing programmes.

      Verbatim31 words
      Experience is indeed a great teacher and we are open to ideas, like Mr Hoe's, that can bolster our existing range of programmes to guide our students in their educational journeys.

    • He offered a different perspective on the aspect of the Motion that not having the perfect fit at 16 means it could be too late.

      Verbatim34 words
      But I would also like to gently offer a different perspective on one aspect of Mr Hoe's Motion – that is not having the perfect fit at 16 means it could be too late.

    • He said MOE has a three-pronged approach to supporting students to discover interests and strengths, develop potential and choose post-secondary pathways.

      Verbatim28 words

    • He said polytechnics and ITE offer three-day Applied Learning Modules.

      Verbatim9 words
      polytechnics and ITE offer three-day Applied Learning Modules (ApLMs)

      Verbatim15 words
      MOE's Opportunity Fund also provides financial support to enable such students to access development opportunities.

    • He said Pathfinder Plus has Secondary 3 and 4 students from disadvantaged backgrounds attend workshops curated according to their strengths.

      Verbatim23 words
      Through MOE's Pathfinder Plus programme, Secondary 3 and 4 students from disadvantaged backgrounds attend workshops that MOE curates according to the students' strengths.

    • He said under MSF's ComLink+ programme, SSO family coaches and FSC case workers work with lower-income families with children below 21.

      Verbatim41 words

    • He said finding the right post-secondary path does not have to happen all at once or perfectly on the first try.

      Verbatim29 words

      Verbatim31 words
      Hock Yang initially wanted to follow in his brother's footsteps into Aerospace Engineering, but soon realised that it was not his cup of tea while pursuing a diploma in that field.

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.
